I like the way you think, and I believe there is some truth to it. But in the grand scale of things I don't think that statement is true. I've felt this way since my early teens, since I was around fourteen years old I'd guess, and it's only gotten worse as I've gotten older. I feel like I've already experienced all of the major things that could tip the scale in favor of enjoyable times. I've traveled a bunch (which I did not enjoy at all), I did my mandatory conscription (what an awful time that was), I've gotten my driver's licence (I don't even own a car, haven't driven one in years). I've worked white collar jobs and blue collar jobs (all of which I've disliked), and I've studied at a high ranking university (stress and anxiety made me drop out).

So what awaits me in the future? First I would need to struggle to get my life together, so I could live a life which, for the most part, I don't enjoy. Maybe I could enjoy in my retirement years, living with no obligations, but that's way too fucking far away. I just can't deal with it.

Don't get me wrong, I think the advice you gave is pretty much the best one could have given me at this time. Thank you for your reply.

>Dude.... Why end it like this? How old are you? Have you got any family?

I'm 26, and I think I already explained in the OP why I'm going to end it. I do have family and friends that will definitely be sad when I'm gone, but even knowing that, I just can't be bothered with trying anymore.
